pencereler.0-5: In fog off Newfoundland, the liner Arctic collided with a smaller steamer. It sank
pencereler.5-12: hours later, and only eighty eight people survived. The captain first tried to help the other ship. Then he
pencereler.12-20: found his own hull holed below the waterline. He ran for land, but the engines stopped. There were lifeboats for fewer than
pencereler.20-30: half aboard. Order broke down, and crew took many of the places. All the women and children aboard died.

segmentler.metin: The SS Arctic sank after a collision in fog off Newfoundland.
It took only a collision in intermittent fog at full speed.
So how could a collision in intermittent fog at full speed do this?
The answer is hull damage below the waterline and lifeboats for fewer than half aboard — and it is why public outrage fed demands for lifeboats and discipline at sea.
